turns.speaker: RUFUS
turns.text: The employee analogy imports all sorts of assumptions — about the agent understanding consequences, about the agent knowing when something feels wrong, about the agent flagging ambiguous instructions. None of those apply.

turns.speaker: JAMIE
turns.text: And in finance, where an agent making an unexpected decision can have systemic consequences — not just one wrong email, but cascading market effects — the relaxation is extremely costly.

turns.speaker: ALEX
turns.text: Systemic risk is the technical term there. It means one failure that triggers a chain of other failures across the whole financial system. The 2008 financial crisis is the most well-known example of what systemic risk looks like when it goes wrong.
